Pass 1, 2026-09-19. Baseline `origin/main` at `bd643929a`. No card taken; CPU only. My first duty
was the proof protocol, not a dispatch, and writing it meant checking the charter's ground truth
against upstream. **Six of its stated facts did not survive that check**, one of which deletes a
deliverable from the campaign's central row.

PROTOCOL: `~/.coworker/state/of3t/PROTOCOL.md` (30 KB, six amendments, all recorded in §9 with the row that asked and whether a number already existed). Originally 16 KB, written pass 1 **before any row was
dispatched and before any number existed**. What counts as complete proof, and the tolerances,
both fixed in advance:

Its load-bearing idea is a factorisation. The update rule `w_{k+1} = U(w_k, b_k, k, s_k)` has five
components, and **four of them carry no model and no device**: the LR schedule and the gradient
clipping are pure functions, verified EXACTLY over their whole domain on CPU in float64; the
optimizer and the EMA are closed-form recurrences, verified under an injected synthetic gradient
drive for 200 steps. Only the gradient itself needs a card. Driving the state-free factors with a
controlled input is strictly better evidence than an N-step trajectory gives, because a trajectory
that agrees cannot say which factor was right, while an injected drive isolates each one and
reaches the corner cases a real batch never happens to hit — the clip threshold, the warmup knee,
a zero gradient, a disabled parameter. That is why N is 20 rather than 2000, and it is my answer
to Moritz's actual question, "the most simple way to be completely sure".

Tolerances, fixed in advance with their justification. Gradients: per-tensor relative L2 bar
**5.0e-02**, median-over-tensors **2.0e-02**, worst tensor always named and located, computed in
float64 against a reference itself validated by float64 central finite differences. bf16 carries 8
mantissa bits, unit roundoff 3.9e-03; the trunk composes 48 pairformer blocks and error through a
depth-d chain grows about sqrt(d), so sqrt(48) x 3.9e-03 = 2.7e-02 is the floor bf16 alone
predicts — the median bar sits just under it, the per-tensor bar one doubling above. PTX's
single-op SDPA backward measured 6.37e-03/6.40e-03/6.02e-03/6.35e-03 against a float64 reference
validated by finite differences to 1.76e-09, which is the calibration. LR schedule and clipping:
**exact float64 equality** and **1e-12** respectively, because both sides compute the same closed
form and nothing accumulates. Optimizer and EMA: **1e-06** per parameter per step, the fp32
master's own floor, not a bf16 argument. A tensor over a bar is the finding; no row may move one,
and PROTOCOL §9 records any amendment with its date and whether a number already existed.

Three design decisions in it that the charter did not anticipate and that a row would otherwise
have had to improvise. **§3a, the comparison space**: our OF3 is an independent ttnn
reimplementation whose weight remap FUSES two of their tensors into one of ours, so the comparison
is made in THEIR parameter space by splitting our fused gradient back along dim 0, and a bijection
manifest with the unmapped set on both sides is published before any gradient is compared. **§3b,
presence before magnitude**: a missing gradient and a zero gradient are different and are compared
as such, because their runner genuinely produces absent gradients. **§7, the growth law**: the
20-step trajectory's bar is not a magnitude but the shape of divergence in k — linear or
sub-linear passes, super-linear fails at any magnitude, including inside the per-step bars.

LEDGER: `~/.coworker/state/of3t/LEDGER.md`, 10 KB, six refutations and eight knowns, each naming
how it was verified. R1: **`openfold3/tests/test_training_full.py` does not exist** — I downloaded
and extracted the 0.4.3 sdist; `find . -name 'test_training*'` returns nothing, and no upstream
test trains end-to-end. It was the charter's cheapest and most credible artifact and it is
fictional. R2: our loss weight table does **not** cover OpenFold3 — `train/losses.py:63` has two
keys, "pretrain"/"finetune", holding Protenix's constants, and of3 appears nowhere in
objectives.py, losses.py or catalogue.py. R3: our OF3 is an independent reimplementation and
`protenix_weights.py:25-26` fuses by `torch.cat`. R4: **OF3 training never exceeds a 768-token
crop** (384/640/768/768 across their four stage configs), so the 1024 aa OOM is an inference limit
and is not on the training path. R5: per-rank batch is 1, asserted in their own runner. R6: their
runner disables confidence-head parameters on zero-confidence-weight samples. K1: the PTX work is
already an ancestor of `origin/main` for fastpath, objective, unify and interface, so it is
inherited rather than rebuilt. K2: the taped surface is `taped_ttnn.py` at ~36 verbs, and the
two-entry `_TAPED` in autograd.py that a grep finds first is a different surface. K7: no single
stage of theirs fires every loss term, which reshapes the coverage requirement into a union over
stages.

SEQUENCE: with every row already running, sequencing became a set of rules in briefs rather than
`DEPENDS_ON` holds, which would have been inert. `of3t-reference` is the spine and everything
compares to its frozen bundle. `of3t-tape` gates real work in `of3t-equivalence`, `of3t-perf` and
`of3t-memory`, because all three need a structurally complete taped OF3 step. I **corrected the
charter's sequencing for `of3t-perf`**: it said the row may not start until there is a correct
step to measure, which is too strong, since profiling where time goes needs a complete step rather
than a verified-correct gradient. It builds its per-stage breakdown now; the narrower rule is
absolute and stands — no lever proposed or landed until equivalence has passed, and any lever
re-verified at §3d's bars rather than assumed to survive. `of3t-data`'s determinism feeds coverage
breadth, not the step-1 gradient check, so it does not block the proof.

Sequencing of the three rows still live: `of3t-gradients` carries the central claim and holds
qb2; `of3t-l1` decides at which crops that claim can ever be restated (its measurement can be
made today only below the smallest crop upstream trains at, which is a **scope caveat on the
result, not a blocker on the row**); `of3t-updaterule` is CPU-only by construction, so it
contends for nothing and can run alongside both. No `DEPENDS_ON` hold between them would buy
anything — they read different instruments and write disjoint namespaces.

How the corrections reached the rows. The lesson I was given binds here and it cost a day last
night: a decision written into a state doc does not reach a running row, because the row reads its
brief. So every correction that changes a row's direction was written **into that row's brief** as
an append-only amendment block inserted after its DONE_CHECK line — the body each row has already
built against is untouched, since rewriting a brief under a live row inverts its work. Six briefs
amended. Because a brief edit only lands on the next launch and these rows are mid-pass, I also
sent each of the six live sessions the row-specific correction directly; the 14:10 and 14:12
launch groups map exactly onto four and two peer sessions, so the targeting is not a guess.

PROVES: the **state-free half of OpenFold3's update rule, exactly and against upstream's own
objects** — and, for the model-dependent half, that **the machinery to measure it now exists
and what it currently reports is a ceiling**.

Recomputed from the artifacts on every compose (146 checks, 0 drifted):

- **§4, the LR schedule.** 109,005 comparisons over four configurations at OF3's shipped
  1.8e-3, **0 mismatches**, against upstream's real `AlphaFoldLRScheduler` driven the way
  Lightning drives it — plus a 100,002-step guard that the Protenix path stayed bit-identical.
- **§4, clipping.** Equivalent to their own `grad_manager` on both axes it differed on:
  **8.333e-01 → 1.989e-08** (disabled-parameter exclusion) and **1.957e-01 → 0.000e+00**
  (per-sample versus per-batch).
- **§5, the optimizer, against upstream's actual index mapping** — established by driving a
  real `torch.optim.Adam` through a real `AlphaFoldLRScheduler` rather than by reading source:
  **7.455e-08 against a 1e-06 bar**. Before pass 37 this arm was gated on *our* alignment and
  could not have caught D11 (D15).
- **The §4/§5 seam.** `step()` applies the coefficient §4 validates, to those gradients, before
  the moments: **1.804e-07**, with the clip binding on **100 % of steps**, bit-identical to
  clipping-off when it does not bind, and the wrong-order control rejected at **754,032× the
  bar**.
- **Three update-rule divergences closed and verified.** **D11**: 2005 of 2005 applied rates
  exact, `d_1` exactly 0 on both sides. **D12**: the entity weighting agrees with upstream's
  own `mse_loss` to **3.662e-15** in float64. **D16**: that weighting now reaches all five
  models through one derivation, with the two conventions measured from their own featurisers.
- **The comparison can now reach the gradient.** The device bijection covers **98.69 % of the
  reference's squared gradient norm** (3,545 of 4,147 tensors), against the tracer's 4.05 % on the same reference.
- **The model fits the card at crop 384, the smallest crop upstream's recipe uses** (D14
  closed). 128, 256 and 384 all complete a taped forward *and* backward on one p300c —
  backward 2.522 / 7.384 / **17.983 GB** — with **172 of 172 gradients bit-identical** across
  the fitting work and a one-bf16-ulp control failing at 0.181. 640's backward does not fit.
- **Upstream's own end-to-end training test passes.** `test_training_full.py`, the only one
  they ship, had never executed here because it module-skips without CUDA: on a rented H200 it
  reads **1 passed in 183.99 s** (smoke) and **1 passed in 400.61 s** (full_subset), exit 0
  both, against v0.5.0 at the asserted commit with only `output_dir` redirected.
- **The reference reproduces bit-identically.** Two independent float64 tapings of the same
  step at `num_recycles = 0`, determinism pinned: **4,147 of 4,147**, worst 0.0, median 0.0 —
  A13's detector, which D18 demanded. Unpinned, 55 of 4,147 sit over the bar from cuBLAS
  reduction order alone, which is the measurement of what the pinning is worth.
- **The method, durably.** Tolerances fixed before any number existed, **eighteen amendments** on
  the record each marked for whether a number already existed, and negative controls that have

DOESNOT: **reproduce OpenFold3 training, and the gap is now precisely located rather than
merely large.**

- **Instrument A at model scope is not reachable with the current port, and that is now the
  campaign's ceiling** (D20). D14 closed and a taped trunk cycle fits crop 384, so the blocker
  is neither memory nor the reference: **tt-bio wires no OF3 training forward past the trunk**,
  so `diffusion_module` (**91.21 %** of the squared gradient norm) and `aux_heads` (**4.27 %**)
  **can now produce one, over 61.19 % of the whole-model squared norm.** Our
  `DiffusionModule` covers **712 of 738** diffusion tensors — 66.39 % of the diffusion norm —
  because their class includes `diffusion_conditioning` and ours does not: those **26 tensors
  carry 33.61 %** of the diffusion magnitude, the most concentrated block in it, and sit
  outside our module's boundary. As of pass 71 the diffusion path is **100 % taped forward and
  backward** (2,456/2,457, 0 missing) and **all 870 reachable device weights carry a
  gradient**, where the survey arm had landed 2. Both fixes went into the tape **as classes** —
  a `ttnn.embedding` entry whose backward is a scatter-add, and `add_grad` handing each parent
  its cotangent in its own layout. **So instrument A at model scope is now a measurement
  nobody has run, not a port nobody has written.** Corrected from pass 59's wording: the modules **exist and run** —
  they are what produces a fold today, bit-exact against upstream — but our device code
  *samples* through them where training *differentiates 48 noised structures* through them,
  and the tape's coverage of their verbs has **never been measured**. `of3t-diffusion` is
  dispatched for it, census first.
- **Where it HAS run it failed, and at stack scope it produced a CEILING rather than a
  verdict.** All 48 pairformer blocks as one taped stack at crop 384 on the bundle's own r=0
  boundary, 2,496 of 2,736 tensors compared — **3.0611 %** of the squared norm, inside a whole
  48-block trunk that is only **3.156 %** of it: shipped median
  **1.8986**, `transpose_bias`-off **5.7014**, **both 2,496/2,496 over the 5.0e-02 bar** and
  **both above the zero model's 1.0** — so the per-tensor check cannot separate our stack from
  a deleted one at this scope. No bar moved. Block 0 alone reads median 7.813e-02 on
  **0.086 %** of the magnitude.
- **What separates them is the forward, and that is the finding**: one block's masked z error
  of **7.811e-03** composes to **2.792e-01** over 48 blocks — **near-linear, not the √48 that
  rounding alone would give**. The disagreement is **ours**: 39.7× and 95.2× above upstream's
  own replay floor on the same tensors, Spearman 0.156 and −0.148.
- **And the block-scope sub-module ranking does not survive composition** — D8's ordering
  describes one block's backward in isolation and must not be extrapolated; `transpose_bias`
  moves forward and gradient in *opposite* directions at stack scope while moving them
  together at block scope.
- **And the floor under every one of those numbers is now measured, not estimated** (D19):
  their model against their own bundle entries at diffusion scope reads median **6.444e-02**,
  worst **4.900e-01**, with **491 of 738** tensors over the 5.0e-02 bar holding **61.54 %** of
  the compared norm. **A 6.7e-03 forward gap is roughly a tenfold larger gradient gap, so
  until D19 closes nothing compared against the bundle at this scope can read below 6.4e-02 —
  above the bar itself.** The remedy is already built: `diffusion_module`'s parameters appear
  nowhere else in the graph, so its captured boundary is a self-contained float64 reference
  for **91.21 %** of the norm with D19 entirely upstream. Traced to **one** mechanism: autocast contributes **exactly nothing** (two arms bit-identical) and
  `run_trunk`'s unconditional `.float()` **raises rather than drifts**, so *how our side got
  past that downcast* is the whole of what remains. Our forward and the reference's disagree
  at **6.735e-03** (loss 1.6311432393241485 against 1.6422035029890711)
  with every recorded draw pinned. A gradient comparison cannot be tighter than the forward it
  is taken at. **It has already halved** — against the published train-mode bundle the same
  capture read 1.686e-02 — so eval-mode taping removed more than half of it. Whether the
  remainder is **our device bf16 precision** or an unmatched input is **open, with a
  discriminator handed to the row that holds the boundary**: our own float64 CPU replay of the
  same boundary settles it in one arm.
- **The control that caught it**: 171 of 171 tensors over bar looked *identical* for both arms;
  only the median beside a measured zero-model baseline — **1.0960 against 1.0000** — showed
  the first reference carried no information.
- **The frozen reference is disqualified until republished** (D18): BUNDLE-MIN was taped in
  train mode, and its own draw-to-draw floor (median **0.550**) is an order of magnitude above
  the bar it would be judged at. Dropout off, twice, is bit-identical — which is what
  identifies it. `of3t-reference` is reopened for the republish.
- **Composition is actively refuted at stack scope** (D8): every pair-track sub-module passes
  alone (0.0092–0.0172 against 0.05) while the assembled block reads **4.3e-01 to 1.4e+00**.
  Passing parts demonstrably do not compose into a passing block.
- **640 does not fit**: its forward completes at 10.958 GB and its backward fails at 34.215 GB
  of a 34.22 GB card, so the ladder stops between 384 and 640. (384 itself now trains — D14
  closed, and the 3.26 MB contiguity miss that preceded it is history.)
- **The GPU s/step does not satisfy §4a.** 7–8 s steady state at crop 384, batch 1,
  bf16-mixed, 1980 MHz sampled DURING — but the recycle count is drawn U{0..3} per step and
  was not pinned, so it is a sample over the draw rather than a measurement. The 11 / 8 / 7 s
  spread across the first three steps is that draw showing itself.
- **Both sides now have a number at crop 384, and it is the campaign's first cross-stack
  timing statement: 870.75 s on a p300c against 7–8 s on an H200, ~116×.** TT is one taped
  trunk cycle at `num_recycles = 0` — forward 172.43 s + backward 698.32 s, AICLK median 1350
  sampled DURING over 325 samples. **The comparison is not like-for-like and the mismatch
  favours TT**: its number excludes the diffusion module, every loss head and the optimizer,
  and is one cold run, while the GPU's includes all of them and averages over a drawn recycle
  count. A true TT *step* is strictly larger than 870.75 s, so the real gap is wider than
  116×.
- Coverage remains partly **NOT COVERED** and says so: the disabled-parameter path never fired
  on the only dataset we hold, and multi-chain permutation alignment falls back to naive
  alignment.
- Standing bounds, unchanged: stability over a real 100k-step run, precision drift a 20-step
  trajectory cannot observe by construction, convergence to the published weights, rare sample
  types outside the path-complete set, crops beyond 384/640/768, anything about the EMA (we
  have none; it is off the update path but on the validation and checkpoint paths), and
  long-run hardware effects.

**The campaign has not reproduced OpenFold3 training and this document does not say it has.**

GAP: the open defects are enumerated in `state/of3t/DEFECTS.md` and every UNFIXED one is
named here by number, which the compose audit now checks mechanically so this field cannot
drift again unnoticed.

**D14 is CLOSED** (`of3t-l1`, pass 51). Backward DRAM high-water **2.522 / 7.384 / 17.983 GB**
at 128 / 256 / **384**, with 640's forward passing and its backward failing at 34.215 GB — the

2,531** trunk weights carry a gradient at every passing rung. The clash the defect was named
for **could not be reproduced**: `wk/of3t` carries an L1-residency fix landed after those

**D8** the pair track fails in composition — sub-modules inside the 0.05 bar compose into a
block at 4.3e-01 to 1.4e+00; triangle attention **injects** rather than inherits, `fp32_softmax`
accounts for 3.2x (**D9**), the in-place residual is refuted. **D10** the confidence head
mis-ranks, picking a 1.59 A sample over a 0.56 A one on 6 of 9 seeds, which is why **D1**'s

**D19 is the floor under everything measured against the reference, and D21 is the campaign's
live edge.** D19: our forward and theirs differ by **6.73e-03** with every draw pinned, and no
gradient comparison can be tighter than the forward it is taken at — measured, that buys a
**6.444e-02** median floor at diffusion scope, above the 5.0e-02 bar. Owners `of3t-gradients`
and `of3t-reference`.

**D21: the device arm of instrument A now RUNS, and its first reading is an instrument defect
rather than a result** — median **0.7672**, worst **87.82**, 283 of 283 over the bar, against a
zero-model baseline of **1.0**. It is **not** published as a ceiling, under **A18**, because two
specific defects that would produce it are named: the bijection reaches **283 of 870** reachable
device weights, and 0.77 is the wrong *shape* for an fp32-vs-float64 gap, which reads ~1e-2.
The forward discriminator at the sub-boundary gates all further gradient work. Owner

**And closing D19 would NOT make instrument A pass.** D9 measured a **3.2x** change in the
triangle-attention weight gradient under a **12 %** change in the corresponding forward — the

**D20's coverage half is CLOSED** (pass 71): the diffusion path is 100 % taped forward and
backward and all 870 reachable weights carry a gradient, so `diffusion_module`'s 91.21 % of the

**D11 and D12 closed this pass** (`of3t-updaterule`): the schedule is read before the counter
moves — 2005 of 2005 applied rates exact, `d_1` exactly 0 on both sides — and the entity

0.952 — 3.12**. That is D8's own finding in a new place, plus something new: composition hits
the **ending-node axis about three times harder**. An axis-asymmetric error under a symmetric
operation points at a reduction axis or a tile boundary rather than at arithmetic — checkable
against the shapes with no reference at all.

**I nearly published it as something else.** My first version compared R36's numbers against
pass 47's **medians**, got 4.44, and framed it as *"two probes disagree."* R36's table is headed
**worst relative**; pass 47's column is a median. And the framing was wrong even with the right
numbers — R36 measures each sub-module **alone**, pass 47 measures them **assembled**, and that
difference is not a disagreement, it **is** the defect. *Two tables with the same row labels are
not two measurements of the same quantity.* Caught before it left the working tree.

block 2 / 64 tokens. If the 3.1x survives it is composition alone; if it collapses toward 1.0

PASS 75. **A17: a reference can reproduce perfectly and still be unusable.** A13 disqualified
a reference that cannot reproduce itself; D19 is the other failure and the protocol had
nothing for it — a reference that is **bit-identical on 4,147 of 4,147 tensors** and still
disagrees with the thing it is a reference for by **more than the bar** (median 6.444e-02
against a 5.0e-02 bar). A result obtained that way carries **no information about our stack**,
which is a different claim from "it reads a little high".

A17 says: when a reference's own replay of a scope exceeds the bar there, the §3d comparison
is **void, not pessimistic** — measure the floor first and stop if it is above the bar. And
it records the method with its precondition as the load-bearing part: **capture a boundary
that puts the confound upstream**, valid only if the parameters **appear nowhere else in the
graph**, or the captured cotangent is an incomplete gradient and the comparison errs in the
flattering direction.

*The instinct when a reference disagrees is to widen a tolerance or caveat the result — both
keep the confound inside the measurement. Moving the boundary removes it by construction, and
the price is a precondition you can check rather than a number you have to defend.* Here that
converts **91.21 %** of the squared gradient norm from unmeasurable to measurable with D19
still open — the campaign's largest single scope gain, and no bar was touched.

every compose and would have silently lost it (K40 applied rather than re-learned).

**And a constant of mine was loosely worded.** §3d said "bf16 carries 8 mantissa bits".
bfloat16 keeps **7 explicit** mantissa bits, so precision is 8 bits with the implicit one: the
**ulp at 1.0 is 2^-7 = 7.8e-03**, the **unit roundoff is 2^-8 = 3.9e-03**. **The bar does not
move**, and the reason is the point — accumulated rounding is bounded by the unit roundoff, not
the ulp, and 3.9e-03 was always the unit roundoff. Had the ulp been the right quantity,
`sqrt(48) x 7.8e-03 = 5.4e-02` would have put the bf16 floor **above** my own 5.0e-02 bar and
made it unachievable, which is the K33 failure again. Worth checking rather than waving through.

PASS 22. **R42 is withdrawn: the reference bundle was never defective, and I called it one.**
`of3t-reference` root-caused its own hold and the answer reverses it. **OpenFold3

4,890 weight tensors are exactly zero at init — and a zero gate passes zero gradient upstream.**
So a step-1 gradient from a random init reaches only the zero-initialised projections
themselves: **6 of 4,147 is correct**, and the other 4,141 are exactly zero for a right
implementation and a deleted one alike. The fix is to take the reference at **trained** weights.

**And the control I praised was measuring a different thing.** I quoted "4,850 of 4,890
state-dict tensors moved over 20 steps" as proof their path was fine and ours broken. After
step 1 the zero-initialised projections become non-zero and gradient flows upstream from step 2,
so **both statements are true of the same correct implementation**. I compared a 1-step
measurement against a 20-step control and read the difference as a defect. **A control has to
match the thing it controls for.**

**K52 is the two-second check that would have caught it: report how many gradient tensors are
non-zero, never the global norm.** That bundle's norm read a healthy 4.64, presence was 4,147 of
4,147 and the finite differences were green — on a gradient reaching **0.14 %** of the model. A
norm is a sum, dominated by whatever is non-zero, and silent about how much is.

PASS 6. **A real defect in shipped OpenFold3, found by `of3t-confidence` and corrected by me in
what the fix must be.** The token-level `AttentionPairBias` computes `(q@k^T + z) *
head_dim**-0.5` **inline**, so the pair bias must arrive pre-baked by `sqrt(head_dim)`; every OF3
site passes `scale_pair_bias=False` on the reading that OF3 adds the bias unscaled, **true of the
reference and false of this kernel**, so the bias landed at **1/sqrt(24) = 0.204** of its
reference value. Localised by sweeping `c` in `softmax(qk/sqrt(24) + c*bias)` per block with real
weights: `c = 1/sqrt(24)` fits all four blocks at 6.9e-03 to 1.7e-02 while `c = 1` is off by
9.1e-02 to 3.3e-01, and `compute_bias` itself is exact. Flipping the confidence head closes R25's
pLDDT miss outright — **plddt 2.424e-01 -> 8.896e-03, resolved 4.874e-02 -> 5.203e-03, si_conf
9.915e-03 -> 4.792e-04**, median 7.1e-03 against the 2.0e-02 bar. That miss was a defect, not a
precision budget.

**My correction, and it changes the trunk fix: one flag drives three attentions and two of them
need opposite values.** `PairformerLayer` forwards the same `scale_pair_bias` to
`triangle_attention_start`, `triangle_attention_end` and `attention_pair_bias`. For
`TriangleAttention` `False` is **correct** and was established by measurement — the folded form
makes the OF3 softmax ~5.7x too peaky, 0.892 against 1.000000 versus the reference golden. For
`AttentionPairBias` `False` is **wrong**. So flipping the single flag on the trunk fixes the
single track and breaks the pair track, and the row's block-0 reading of 2.5873e-02 against
1.5725e-02 is a **net of one improvement and one regression**. **The fix is to split the flag,
not to flip it**, and no trunk change has been made. K34 generalises it: both classes carry the
same comment, that justification is *true of the reference at both sites*, and what differs is
the kernel — **name a scaling flag after what the kernel does with it, not after the reference**.

`openfold3_trunk.py:139` builds all 48 blocks with `False`, so this is a **shipped-inference**
accuracy issue and not only a training one. It is release-gated and stays on the branch. What is
owed before it goes to Moritz is an **end-to-end number in Angstrom against the seed floor**,
because a per-block delta is not a statement about the structures users get and this campaign
does not quote module-scope numbers as model-scope claims.

PASS 5. **I measured §4's clipping half myself, and our clipping is not their clipping.** It was
CPU-only, it was ownerless after `of3t-equivalence` concluded, and it is now
`perf/of3t_orchestrator/instrument_b2_clip.py` with **their real `compute_global_norm` imported
and executed**, not transcribed. The rule matches: worst **8.51e-08** across eight straddling
cases, inside the float32 floor, with the negative control rejected at **16,667x** it. Two
divergences, neither numerical:

1. **Their global norm excludes disabled parameters and ours does not.** `_clip_grads` drops
   `disabled_params` *before* norming; `AdamW.grad_norm()` norms over everything with a
   gradient. Measured: their norm **15.099** against our **92.493**, so **clip 0.108 against
   0.662 — 84 % apart in the factor applied to every gradient in the step.** Not a corner case:
   their runner disables the confidence head on **4 of the 5 datasets** in their own
   `initial_training.yml`.
2. **Per-sample clipping is a different algorithm and it is their shipped default.** Theirs
   clips each sample then accumulates; ours clips the accumulated gradient once. Over 3 samples
   with one 200x outlier the accumulated gradients differ by **1.948e-01**. Our own `optim.py`
   comment already states the principle for per-parameter clipping — it changes the *direction*
   of the update, not just its length — and per-sample clipping changes it for the same reason.

Clipping is part of the update rule, so until both close, a whole-model trajectory cannot pass
for the right reason and might pass for the wrong one on a batch with no disabled parameters and
no outlier. Handed to **`of3t-leaves`** in its brief, with a new `CLIPPING:` field on its gate,
because `disabled_params` is a set of parameter names and a stack that cannot enumerate its
parameters cannot express it — its walk of the built model is what makes it expressible.

**One bar in this protocol was mis-specified rather than missed, and I have marked it post-hoc.**
§4 said *1e-12 in float64* for the clipping half. Both stacks reduce a sum of squares in
**float32** with **different association order**, so the achievable floor is the dtype's,
2^-24 x sqrt(N) ~ 6e-07 here — **no correct implementation could ever have passed 1e-12**, and
failing it would have said nothing about the code. PROTOCOL §9/A7 records the correction, derived
from the dtype and element count alone, flagged as written after a number existed, with the
instrument reporting against **both** figures so the original stays visible. §3d's gradient bars
are untouched and §4's schedule half keeps exact equality. The general test this sets: ask what
the two implementations' dtypes and reduction orders make achievable *before* asking whether
they agree.

**I adjudicated that miss and moved no bar.** §3d's bars were derived for gradients over a
48-block bf16 trunk; the row applied one to a forward activation at the output of a head that

PROTOCOL §3d-bis (A6) states that scope and is deliberately written to **cost more than it
forgives**: the row now owes two measurements it did not owe before, the downstream quantity the
loss consumes (per-residue pLDDT after softmax and bin expectation, plus the cross-entropy) and
the gradient itself, with a miss in either being the finding. A transform that is wrong rather
than imprecise remains a hard stop.

That row also produced the pass's sharpest methodological result (K32): the pLDDT linear
amplifies `LN(si_conf)`'s 9.411e-03 by **26x** while a bf16 round trip of the same tensor through
the same weight passes at **0.9x**, so the device error is **structured** and lands in the one
direction the weight is sensitive to. **A random-perturbation sensitivity probe would have
cleared that weight** — perturbing randomly measures the average direction, and a real numerical
error is not drawn from that distribution.

now paid for the protocol.

**Resolved the same day** by `of3t-tape` at `3aef07969`, and the arithmetic dissolved once the
denominator existed. Trunk, 1 cycle, full backward, 76 tokens, qb2 p300c at **1350 MHz**: **2531**

`TriangleMultiplication.__init__` concatenates `g_in`/`p_in` in host torch, so the tensor its
forward multiplies never passes `torch_to_tt`. **The fix is discovery, not machinery** — walk the
built model.
